title: PixelKin - Title Theme (Lanterns in the Dark)
_note: The iconic title-screen riff under the logo + New Game/Continue/Settings. gbc house style (4-voice band) for seamless cohesion with the Tinderwick 'Lantern Lullaby' (same C-major/A-minor world, same pulse25 lead + pulse12 music-box arp + tri_bass hearth pulse + near-absent noise tick). 96 BPM, 4/4. The loop PROUDLY states the Vesper motif (G3->C4->D4 lift, overshooting; E4->D4->C4 settle home) up front and warm-but-wistful, then lifts it an octave for the 'proud' B-statement, with a homesick A-minor turn before resolving home. 16-bar loop body (~24s at 96 BPM). Last bar voice-leads G2(dom)->C downbeat so the loop seam is seamless (no dead-stop tonic). Slightly brighter and more confident than the town lullaby (this is the title fanfare-ish statement), but unmistakably the same tune the player will hear when they reach Tinderwick.
key: C major (wistful turn to A minor)

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: A: proud full Vesper statement (G3->C4->D4 ... E4->D4->C4), a touch more dotted/confident than the lullaby. A': the motif lifted an octave (G4->C5->D5 ... E5->D5->C5) - the 'sky' statement, the proud peak of the riff. B: A-minor homesick answer (the catch in the throat) walking up F4->G4 toward the dominant. A'': resolve home, the leap settling firmly to C, then a small turn down to G3 so the line lifts back into bar 1.

tracks._note: Slow music-box broken-chord arp (eighths), exactly the lullaby's texture so the two themes are siblings. C-E-G under major, G-B-D under the dominant cadence; the octave-up A' brightens to C-G-C-E sparkle; A-C-E under the A-minor turn, F-A-C / G-B-D under the answer.

tracks.name: bass
tracks._note: Warm rocking root-fifth 'hearth' pulse, two half-notes per bar - the lullaby's bass. Walks A->E and F->G under the B-section. Final bar holds G2->G2 (dominant) to voice-lead into the C downbeat of bar 1: seamless seam.

tracks.name: drums
tracks._note: Near-absent, like the lullaby: a soft noise tick on each bar downbeat (one hat + a half-rest's worth of silence = 4 beats), with a gentle offbeat hat on the proud octave-up A' section to lend the title a little shine, and a soft fill at the loop seam so the repeat breathes. Each bar = 4 beats.
